lower_bound.witness: COUNTEREXAMPLE to the stated algebraic identity: take t=1, c=0, y=1, b=1. Left side (t+2c+y)^2-4(t+c)(y+b) = (1+0+1)^2 - 4·1·(1+1) = 4-8 = -4. Right side (t-y)^2+4(t+c)(b-c) = 0 + 4·1·(1-0) = +4. So the identity is false; the correct expansion is (t-y)^2+4(t+c)(c-b) (sign of the last term flipped). NON-SEQUITUR: from the line as written, (t-y)^2+4(t+c)(b-c) >= 0 yields c-b <= (t-y)^2/(4(t+c)), i.e. a bound on d(t)-d(y), not the claimed (5) b-c <= (t-y)^2/(4(t+c)). The stated (5) is in fact true under the correct expansion, but it does not follow from what is written.
lower_bound.load_bearing: Inequality (5) is the sole source of the one-sided bound d(y)-d(t) <= (t-y)^2/(4t); (6) only bounds d(t)-d(y). Without (5) the two-sided estimate (7) collapses to one side and the telescoping in Section 3 cannot conclude d(v)=d(u).

parsed.notes: Route: x=f(y) gives f(f(y))=2f(y)-y, d>=0 via iterates, then x=f(t) squared in both inequalities gives quadratic control of d, telescoping forces d constant. Correct answer f(x)=x+C, C>=0. Only defect: sign slip in the AM-GM expansion; stated conclusion (5) is true but not derived from the written line.
